events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.44 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
One off-route segment exists on this RydeTAXI trip: 17:41–17:44, 1.76 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.03 km, adding 1.73 km and straying up to 979 m off route [F3]. Under RD-1 each such segment must independently clear RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5, and any segment that clears none is an unexempt detour [F3][RD-1].

RD-4(a) requires a DataMall incident sitting on the replaced portion of the optimal route, reported before the segment began and still listed during the trip [F12][RD-4]. The trace settles this element as failed for the segment: no qualifying incident is matched to the replaced stretch, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F3][F10][F12][RD-4]. The 17:16 Seletar Expressway report is an expressway-corridor incident at 0 m from "the optimal route" in the abstract [F12], but nothing ties it to the 1.73 km the driver actually abandoned; the parallel corridor was moving at band 5 (40–49 km/h) and the Seletar stretch at band 4 (30–39 km/h), both well above the band 1–2 congestion range [F10][F11][RD-4]. RD-4(b) is expressly corroborative only and cannot exempt by itself, and there is no qualifying (a) for it to corroborate [F10][F11][RD-4]. So the segment is not exempt on reasonable-cause grounds [F3][F12][RD-4].

RD-5 fails as well: the only chat is the rider confirming her pickup spot and the driver naming his car [F7][F8]; there is no driver proposal of a route change before leaving the optimal route and no rider agreement, and the driver's post-hoc statement about "an accident ahead" is a statement that cannot supply the missing pre-departure agreement against the GPS record [F7][F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. claims.assertion: The trip ran 19.3 km against a 17.3 km optimal route (+2.1 km, +12%), so the rider was billed for distance the shortest-direct-route duty did not permit.
The GPS track contains one off-route segment (17:41–17:44) of 1.76 km where the optimal route covers only 0.03 km, adding 1.73 km and straying up to 979 m off the optimal route; no clause exempts it.

The driver's claimed accident justification is not corroborated for the segment actually replaced: the only traffic incident is on the Seletar Expressway-side corridor and there is no traffic fact showing an incident or band 1–2 blocking the replaced optimal-road segment within 300 m, so RD-4(a) is not met for this off-route segment.

The chat log shows no route-change proposal and no agreement: the rider only confirmed her pickup spot and never consented, so RD-5 does not exempt the deviation (the driver's post-hoc statement is a statement, and the GPS record of the detour wins).

As a RydeTAXI metered trip, the extra kilometres flow straight into the meter: Refund = the 1.73 km unexempt extra_km on F3 × the per-km rate $1.41/km (fare.distance_fare $27.23 ÷ fare.distance_km 19.3, per F6) = $2.44, and the residual 0.37 km of the billed +2.1 km (F1, F4) is not refundable.
Only the 1.73 km unexempt segment is charged; the stop/excess unrelated to it and the $0.00 waiting fee on F6 are outside this claim, so no additional refund is sought.

weaknesses: The other side will rely on F12 (an accident reported 17:16 on the Seletar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route, lanes blocked) plus the 17:41–17:44 timing and F10 (Seletar Expressway speed band 4, 30–39 km/h, during 17:18–18:02) and the driver's F9 statement to argue the deviation was a reasonable-cause reroute under RD-4(a)/(b) — the incident is at 0 m from the optimal route but our route facts do not show the named road, so the judge may read RD-4(a) as satisfied and award no_action.
The extra time (F2: 29.2 min vs 24 min) is not refundable on its own, and F6 shows no waiting fee was charged, so our recoverable amount is limited to the $2.44 distance item computed in C5.
F3 shows only one off-route segment even though F1 shows +2.1 km total, so roughly 0.3–0.4 km of the billed excess (F4) is unmapped residual that RD-2 expressly leaves with the rider.

The rider's profile (F14: 2 disputes in 90 d, 1 upheld) does not support a flag_account request against the driver, and F15 shows the driver has 0 upheld route disputes, weakening any 'repeat offender' framing.

claims.assertion: The single off-route segment (17:41–17:44, +1.73 km, F3) coincides with an accident on the Seletar Expressway that was reported at 17:16, lies 0 m from the optimal route, and was still listed with lanes blocked for the whole trip window — an exact RD-4(a) match.

The diversion is corroborated by objective road conditions: the optimal route's Seletar Expressway stretch ran at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) and Tampines Expressway at band 5 (40–49 km/h) throughout 17:18–18:02, and weather was fair (0.0 mm rain) so congestion was not weather-related.

No rain or weather factor (F13) contributed to the detour, so the only candidate cause is the recorded expressway accident (F12), which is precisely the 'reasonable cause' RD-4 requires for a justified reroute.
Only one gps-detour segment exists (F3), and it is fully exempt under RD-4(a), so under RD-4(c) no segment falls back to RD-2: the driver's route deviation attracts no refund.

The rider's complaint of an unexplained route change (F7–F9 series) is contradicted by the system record: the +12% distance (F1) and +5.6 min (F2) are accounted for by the 1.73 km exempt emergency detour (F3), and system records prevail over statements.

The metered fare components are ordinary for a RydeTAXI trip — distance $27.23 for 19.3 km and time $7.58 for 29.2 min, no surge (1.0×), no waiting fee — so the $40.18 total (F6) contains no unpublished or unjustified add-on under FARE-1.

The excess-distance amount the rider disputes is $2.90 (2.1 km × $1.41/km, F4), and because the underlying segment is exempt the recoverable amount under RD-2 is zero, so the correct outcome for this segment is no_action with no violation recorded.
No flag_account should attach to the driver: he has 831 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (route: 0, no-show: 0), so the 'repeated' precondition of RD-6 is not met.

weaknesses: The off-route segment ran up to 979 m away from the optimal route (F3), which the claimant will argue is more than a minor rejoin and looks like a deliberate detour rather than an incident avoidance.

There is no chat message showing the driver told the rider about the reroute before taking it (F7, F8 only cover the pickup), so the claimant will argue any passenger consent requirement would not be satisfied.
